He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers Scarlet Knights]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2025 NBA draft class. ==Early life and high school career== Bailey grew up in [[Chattanooga, Tennessee]], and initially attended [[Boyd-Buchanan School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.timesfreepress.com/news/2021/jan/11/prep-roundup-freshman-bailey-helps-spark-boy/|title=Prep roundup: Freshman Ace Bailey helps spark Boyd Buchanan past region rival|work=[[Chattanooga Times Free Press]]|date=January 11, 2021|access-date=November 12, 2023}} After his freshman year, he moved to [[Powder Springs, Georgia]], and enrolled at [[McEachern High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.onthebanks.com/2023/11/12/23957630/5-star-forward-ace-bailey-officially-signs-nli-with-rutgers|title=5-Star Forward Ace Bailey Officially Signs NLI with Rutgers|first=John|last=Catapano|website=OnTheBanks.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=November 12, 2023|access-date=November 14, 2023}} Bailey averaged 22 points, 14 rebounds, three assists and four blocks per game as a junior.{{cite web|url=https://rutgers.rivals.com/news/rutgers-scarlet-knights-basketball-signee-bio-f-ace-bailey|title=Rutgers Scarlet Knights Basketball Signee Bio: F Ace Bailey|first=Richard|last=Schnyderite|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=November 12, 2023|access-date=November 15, 2023|archive-date=November 15, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231115160915/https://rutgers.rivals.com/news/rutgers-scarlet-knights-basketball-signee-bio-f-ace-bailey|url-status=dead}} He improved his stats to 32.5 points, 15.5 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.4 blocks per game as a senior. Bailey was selected to play in the [[2024 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2024 McDonald's All-American Game]], [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[Nike Hoop Summit]] during his senior year. ===Recruiting=== Bailey was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2024 class, according to major recruiting services.{{cite basketball|Monmouth]].{{Cite magazine |date=November 15, 2024 |title=How Ace Bailey Fared in His Rutgers' Debut |url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/newsfeed/ace-bailey-2025-nba-draft-rutgers-debut-dylan-harper |access-date=July 8, 2025 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}} On November 20, he recorded his first career [[double-double]] with 23 points and 10 rebounds against [[Merrimack Warriors men's basketball|Merrimack]].{{Cite web |date=November 20, 2024 |title=Ace Bailey's 23-point double-double leads No. 24 Rutgers over Merrimack |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/ncaa-mens-basketball/article/ace-baileys-23-point-double-double-leads-no-24-rutgers-over-merrimack/ |access-date=July 8, 2025 |website=[[Sportsnet]]}} Bailey earned [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] Freshman of the Week honors (alongside [[Kasparas Jakučionis|Kasparas Jakucionis]]) following his career-high 39-point performance against [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] on January 2, 2025.{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2025 |title=Ace Bailey Named Big Ten's Freshman of the Week |url=https://scarletknights.com/news/2025/1/6/mens-basketball-ace-bailey-named-big-tens-freshman-of-the-week.aspx |access-date=July 8, 2025 |website=Rutgers University Athletics}}{{Cite web |date=January 7, 2025 |title=Purdue, Illinois, Rutgers Score Men's Basketball Weekly Accolades |url=https://bigten.org/mbb/article/blt08ad80dff76d3319/ |access-date=July 8, 2025 |website=[[Big Ten Conference]]}} On January 19, he was named Big Ten Freshman of the Week for the second time after leading the team to a 2–0 week and topping the scoring charts with two double-doubles: 20 points and 10 rebounds against [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], and 24 points with 11 rebounds against [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]].{{Cite web |date=January 19, 2025 |title=Ace Bailey Named Big Ten's Freshman of the Week for 2nd Time |url=https://scarletknights.com/news/2025/1/20/mens-basketball-ace-bailey-named-big-tens-freshman-of-the-week-for-2nd-time.aspx |access-date=July 8, 2025 |website=Rutgers University Athletics}} At the conclusion of his freshman year, Bailey declared for the [[2025 NBA draft|2025 NBA Draft]] on April 23, foregoing his remaining college eligibility. He finished his collegiate career having earned third-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] and Big Ten All-Freshman Team honors.{{Cite web |date=April 23, 2025 |title=Men's Basketball's Ace Bailey Declares for 2025 NBA Draft |url=https://scarletknights.com/news/2025/4/23/mens-basketball-mens-basketballs-ace-bailey-declares-for-2025-nba-draft.aspx |access-date=July 8, 2025 |website=Rutgers University Athletics}}{{Cite web |date=April 23, 2025 |title=Bailey entering NBA draft, shares Rutgers 'love' |url=https://www.espn.ph/nba/story/_/id/44815023/ace-bailey-declares-nba-draft-one-year-rutgers |access-date=July 8, 2025 |website=[[ESPN]]}} ==Professional career== Bailey was selected with the fifth overall pick by the [[Utah Jazz]] in the [[2025 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/what-ace-bailey-brings-to-the-utah-jazz|title=What Ace Bailey Brings to the Utah Jazz|website=NBA.com|date=June 25, 2025|access-date=June 26, 2025}} On July 2, he signed with the Jazz with [[Walter Clayton Jr.]]{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-ace-bailey-and-walter-clayton-jr|title=Utah Jazz Sign Ace Bailey and Walter Clayton Jr.|website=NBA.com|date=July 2, 2025|access-date=July 3, 2025}} On January 22, 2026, Bailey recorded a then-career-high 25 points along with 6 rebounds and 3 assists in a game against the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web |title=Ace Bailey Career High 25 Points vs Spurs |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/baileac01.html |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=February 28, 2026}} On February 10, during a game against the [[Atlanta Hawks]], Bailey surpassed the 500-point milestone in his 45th career game. At 19 years and 181 days old, he became the youngest player in Jazz franchise history to reach 500 career points.{{cite web |last=Koch |first=Jared |title=Ace Bailey Makes Utah Jazz History With Career Milestone |url=https://www.si.com/nba/jazz/onsi/news/ace-bailey-makes-utah-jazz-history-with-career-milestone |website=Sports Illustrated |date=February 10, 2026 |access-date=February 28, 2026}} On March 5, Bailey scored a career-high 32 points in a 122–112 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/utah-jazz/jazz-news-nba-acknowledges-ace-baileys-milestone-vs-wizards|title=NBA acknowledges Jazz star Ace Bailey’s personal milestone vs. Wizards|website=ClutchPoints|last=Bhatnagar|first=Rishabh|date=March 5, 2026|access-date=March 5, 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jazzs-ace-bailey-sets-career-high-scoring-mark/|title=Jazz's Ace Bailey: Sets career-high scoring mark|website=CBS Sports|date=March 5, 2026|access-date=March 5, 2026}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2025}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2025–26 Utah Jazz season|Utah]] | 72 || 61 || 27.6 || .443 || .344 || .750 || 4.2 || 1.8 || .8 || .7 || 13.8 |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"|Career | 72 || 61 || 27.6 || .443 || .344 || .750 || 4.2 || 1.8 || .8 || .7 || 13.8 {{S-end}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2024–25]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2024–25 Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball team|Rutgers]] | 30 || 30 || 33.3 || .460 || .346 || .692 || 7.2 || 1.3 || 1.0 || 1.3 || 17.6 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Bailey's mother, Ramika McGee, played college basketball at [[West Virginia University]].{{cite web |title=Airious Bailey - Men's Basketball |url=https://scarletknights.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/airious-bailey/14341 |website=Rutgers University Athletics |access-date=September 25, 2024 |language=en}} Bailey's father, Richard Bailey, played college basketball at Houston. His aunt, [[Venus Lacy]], played in the [[Women's National Basketball Association|WNBA]] and was a member of Team USA's [[Basketball at the 1996 Summer Olympics|1996 Olympic team]] that won a gold medal.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/kentucky/article/ace-bailey-kentucky-basketball-recruiting-offer--193432711/|title=Kentucky offers 2024 5-star forward Ace Bailey|first=Chris|last=Fisher|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=September 15, 2022|access-date=November 14, 2023}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{basketball stats}} *[https://scarletknights.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/airious-bailey/14341 Rutgers Scarlet Knights bio] *[https://www.usab.com/players/ace-bailey USA Basketball bio] {{Utah Jazz current roster}} {{2025 NBA draft}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Bailey, Ace}} [[Category:2006 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Chattanooga, Tennessee]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball players]] [[Category:Small forwards]] [[Category:Utah Jazz draft picks]] [[Category:Utah Jazz players]]
